parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a strongly protective state with a hostile federal layer. State law bans gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations, protects gender-affirming care, imposes no facility restriction, and a July 2026 national assessment groups it as low-risk; protections have survived repeal referenda and court challenges. But federal rules govern entry and custody: a February 2025 cable instructs visa refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered; foreign trans travelers have been detained and eight governments issued advisories. Airports impose outing-prone screening; federal buildings exclude trans users; immigration custody documented abuse. Litigation is unresolved. Entry exposure and conditional custody risk outweigh the state's daily-life protections without reaching imprisonment there.

entry_documents.exposure: February 2025 cable instructs officers to refuse visa cases where documents or other evidence cast reasonable doubt on sex, and to consider fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; X-marker processing halted; documented detentions of foreign trans travelers; 8+ governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiration; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic with limited waivers; civil-liberties union suit pending; state ID marker changes available (resident-facing climate signal).
entry_documents.interaction: Federal entry control gates whether the state's protections ever apply; airline document checks feed the same scrutiny; refusal can escalate to immigration custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented forced-labour programmes, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men; federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for inmates from 2026; foreign trans citizens detained over visa issues.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State prison houses a trans woman per gender identity; state courts function and habeas presumably available; federal custody not automatic for ordinary visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Visa refusal or document discrepancy can escalate into federal immigration custody where the documented abuse occurs; state custody protections do not reach federal facilities.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities (airports, federal buildings); airport secondary screening and pat-downs risk outing every trans traveler; four other states criminalize facility use (not this state).
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no law restricting facility use; 2014 state supreme court ruling required access aligned with gender identity; state-funded buildings are outside the federal ban's direct reach.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules override state protection inside federally funded spaces; the state's open-facilities rule governs state and private settings.

care_services.exposure: Federal executive order frames minors' gender-affirming care as 'mutilation'; October 2025 proposed rule would bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans care (proposed, not in effect); funding threats against institutions.
care_services.protection: State law since April 2024 explicitly protects gender-affirming healthcare; 16-17 year olds may obtain hormones since July 2023; SOGI data mandate from October 2026; conversion therapy on minors banned.
care_services.interaction: A visiting minor's care-seeking in this state is protected by state law; federal funding and insurance rules target residents and institutions more than out-of-pocket visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes identifying and neutralizing groups 'radically pro-transgender'; December 2025 reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' framing; advocates compare the administration to early genocide; 2025 poll shows 66% supporting sex-at-birth document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Dossier notes the reward never uses gender ideology as a criterion and counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute and state gender-identity penalty enhancements apply.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises the probability and severity of scrutiny for visibly trans visitors at federal touchpoints; state law-enforcement remains bound by protective state statutes.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders call minors' care 'mutilation' and direct criminal investigation of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; proposed federal insurance rule pending; a parent could face scrutiny if a minor's presentation draws attention at federal touchpoints.
minors_guardians.protection: State protects minors' gender-affirming care and bans conversion therapy; school-focused enforcement targets institutions, not visiting families; sanctuary-protection bill for transgender minors was set aside in 2024.
minors_guardians.interaction: Visiting minors are unlikely to enter school settings where federal prosecution directives operate; care access during the visit runs through state-protected providers.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence figures or enforcement statistics for the hate-crime enhancement; national bias statistics cover sexual orientation predominantly; social friction from a national majority supporting birth-sex document rules.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gay/trans panic defence abolished 2019; gender-identity hate-crime penalty enhancements; public-accommodations and employment protections operative; police bound by state civil-rights law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State protections give a recourse if bias violence occurs, but the dossier cannot establish current street-level frequency for this state.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal litigation over passports, executive orders and health rules unresolved; no documented working appeal for visa refusal on sex grounds; university sports compliance status and future legislative trajectory unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State courts have ruled for trans people (2014); protections survived two repeal referenda; ACLU suit and legal-aid FAQ provide active challenge infrastructure; state remains in a national low-risk group.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies work within the state but cannot cure federal entry refusal or federal custody; federal outcomes depend on pending courts.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than Vellandra: no blanket trans-visitor exclusion register here — scrutiny targets document discrepancy with waivers, litigation and limited outcomes short of expulsion-only; the state provides full daily-life protections, whereas Vellandra's exclusion is universal with no remedy at all.

Similar on entry (secondary screening, discretionary refusal, slow appeal), but our dossier adds documented immigration-custody abuse (worse) while the state supplies operative anti-discrimination, care and facility protections (better) that Kestrel Isles does not show.

Worse on entry: here the cable instructs sex-based scrutiny rather than prohibiting it, with documented detentions and foreign advisories; better in-country: explicit state protections cover accommodations, care and facilities, where Luskaine's daily-life context is unspecified and remedies were needed per-incident.

Materially below Meridia: its border officers are trained for respectful inspection with tribunal appeals, while our regime instructs refusal on sex doubt, documents detentions, and imposes federal facility exclusion — entry exposure Meridia simply does not carry.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is layered: federal rules dominate entry, airports, federal buildings and immigration custody; state rules dominate daily life, care, and state/private facilities. A trans visitor's journey begins under the hostile federal layer — instructed visa refusal on sex doubt, outing-prone screening, possible detention with documented abuse — before reaching a state whose protections are demonstrably operative (referenda-surviving civil-rights law, no facility ban, protected care, hate-crime enhancements, identity-based prison placement). If discovered during the stay, consequences are friction with recourse; if discovered at the border, refusal and possible fraud findings follow; the severe custody harm is real but conditional. Litigation is unresolved, so exposure varies by moment of travel. Net: reduced but not low risk.
